findings.rationale: CT's uploaded updates are strongly anomalous: over 20 rounds its mean cosine to the median update is -0.52 (noise-adjusted z=-8.4) and its median norm ratio is 2.29 (z=+5.0). The per-round check (eps 0.5, noisy) shows cosine turning strongly negative from about round 5 onward, with norm ratio rising above 1 from round 5. Its local performance is also off: AUC 0.68 (z=-3.3) with CITL -0.06 and ECE z=+4.3, i.e. observed prevalence exceeds predicted risk. Its Sex=0 subgroup has O/E 1.64 (noise-adjusted z=4.2). This pattern fits flipped labels (negatives recorded as positives) rather than poisoning, because the local data and performance are not normal. Onset is estimated from the per-round check; it is not exact.

UT shows the same signature as CT, more strongly. Mean cosine to the median update is -0.53 (z=-8.5), median norm ratio 3.08 (z=+6.3), and min cosine -0.86 (z=-5.5). Local AUC is 0.67 (z=-3.5), CITL is -0.059 (z=-4.4) and ECE is high (z=+4.6), so observed outcomes exceed predicted risk. Subgroup O/E is elevated in both sexes (Sex=1 O/E 1.58, noise-adjusted z=6.1; Sex=0 O/E 1.67). Local data looks wrong, not the upload alone, so this is labelled label_noise rather than poisoning. No per-round check was run for UT, so onset is assumed to be from the start of the run.

VT's updates are anomalous: mean cosine -0.46 (z=-8.0), median norm ratio 2.27 (z=+5.3), min cosine -0.83 (z=-5.3). Local AUC is the lowest in the federation at 0.63 (z=-4.3), with CITL -0.047 (z=-3.5), so observed prevalence exceeds predicted risk. This points to noisy labels rather than poisoning. Subgroup O/E is high in Sex=0 (1.54) and Income group 6 (O/E 4.87, noise-adjusted z=3.2). Evidence is somewhat weaker than for CT and UT, and onset is assumed to be from the start of the run.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then ran narrower confirmations. Three clients (CT, UT, VT) stand apart on several independent tools. Their updates point against the median (negative mean cosine, large norm ratios), and their local AUC is low with CITL negative and high subgroup O/E. Together this fits label noise (flipped outcomes), not poisoning, since local data is also affected. CT's per-round data shows the anomaly from about round 5; onset for UT and VT is assumed from the start because per-round checks were not affordable. Other flags were not confirmed: the VI, WV and GU outliers were not reproduced in narrower queries (the VI Stroke and PhysHlth values and WV AnyHealthcare moved to normal on re-query), and GU's jittery per-round updates come from a small site (n=708) and are not clearly beyond noise. No drift, missing-artefact, subgroup-bias or prevalence-shift findings. Budget was fully spent (0.0 left).
